title: IoT Telemetry Platform
summary: An IoT platform connects millions of small, unreliable devices to the cloud. Each device has its own certificate and publishes sensor readings over MQTT, a lightweight protocol built for flaky networks. A rules engine routes the stream to a time-series database and alerting, and firmware updates flow back out in signed, staged rollouts that can roll back when a device fails to boot.

walkthrough.title: Device connects and publishes
walkthrough.text: A thermostat opens a TLS connection with its X.509 client certificate and publishes readings to devices/th-8812/telemetry every 30 s, buffering locally while offline.

walkthrough.title: Authenticate and authorise
walkthrough.text: The broker checks the certificate against the device registry, then applies a topic policy: this device may only publish under its own ID.

walkthrough.title: Route with rules
walkthrough.text: A rule such as SELECT temp, humidity FROM 'devices/+/telemetry' forwards messages into a stream, where they are validated, enriched with device metadata, and checked for anomalies.

walkthrough.title: Store as time series
walkthrough.text: Readings are written to a time-series database, keeping raw data for days and downsampled 1-minute and 1-hour rollups for years.

walkthrough.title: Visualise and alert
walkthrough.text: Dashboards show fleet health. Alerts fire on thresholds (freezer above -10 °C) or on silence (no data for 10 minutes).

walkthrough.title: Plan a firmware rollout
walkthrough.text: Operators target a cohort from the registry, such as hardware rev B on firmware 2.3, and schedule v2.4 for 1% of them first.

walkthrough.title: Deliver the update over the air
walkthrough.text: Devices download the signed image, verify it, write it to the inactive partition, and reboot into it. If the new firmware fails its health check, the bootloader switches back automatically.

data.label: Devices

output.name: Telemetry
output.type: MQTT QoS 1: { temp: 21.4, rh: 40, batt: 88, ts }

responsibilities: Sample sensors and publish efficiently to save battery and bandwidth.
Buffer readings while offline and resend later.
Apply updates safely with automatic rollback.

failureModes.scenario: Whole fleet reconnects at once after an outage
failureModes.impact: A reconnect storm overwhelms the broker.
failureModes.mitigation: Exponential backoff with random jitter on every device.

failureModes.impact: Readings land at the wrong time.
failureModes.mitigation: Sync time on connect; record both device and server timestamps.

data.label: MQTT Broker
responsibilities: Holds persistent connections cheaply with keep-alives.
Enforces per-device topic permissions.
Queues messages for devices that are briefly offline (persistent sessions).

failureModes.impact: One hacked device can impersonate or listen to others.
failureModes.mitigation: Policy variables bound to the device ID in its certificate.
Clustered brokers behind a load balancer; devices reconnect with jitter.

data.label: Device Registry

input.name: Provisioning
input.type: Factory-issued cert, claimed by an owner

output.name: Identity
output.type: { deviceId, model, hwRev, fw, owner, desired/reported state }

responsibilities: Knows every device, its certificate, owner, and firmware version.
Keeps a 'shadow' of each device's desired and reported state.
Revokes certificates for lost or compromised devices.

failureModes.scenario: Shared credentials baked into all devices
failureModes.impact: One extracted key compromises the whole fleet.
failureModes.mitigation: Unique per-device keys in a secure element, generated at manufacture.
Long-lived device certs with an over-the-air rotation path.

data.label: Rules & Stream Processing
responsibilities: Routes topics to the right downstream systems.
Validates units and ranges and drops corrupt readings.
Detects anomalies and silence in real time.

failureModes.scenario: Malformed payloads from a firmware bug
failureModes.mitigation: Schema validation with a dead-letter stream per firmware version.
Buffer in the stream; process recent data first.

data.label: Time-Series Store

output.name: Queries
output.type: avg(temp) by site, 5-minute buckets, last 7 days

responsibilities: Ingests millions of points per second, written mostly in time order.
Keeps rollups so long-range queries stay fast and cheap.
Applies retention: raw for days, aggregates for years.

failureModes.mitigation: Device ID as a series key, not free-form tags; limit tag sets.

failureModes.impact: Rollups computed before all data arrived.
failureModes.mitigation: Recompute recent buckets as late data lands.

data.label: OTA Update Service
responsibilities: Delivers firmware in stages with automatic halt on failures.
Signs images so devices accept only genuine firmware.
Tracks per-device update status.

failureModes.mitigation: A/B partitions with boot health checks and automatic fallback; tiny first cohort.

failureModes.impact: CDN and cellular data cost spikes.

data.label: Dashboards & Alerts
responsibilities: Shows fleet health: online count, battery, firmware mix.
Alerts on thresholds and on devices going silent.
Gives customers views of their own devices.

failureModes.impact: Thousands of pages during a regional network outage.
failureModes.mitigation: Aggregate alerts by site or region; alert on fleet-wide rates.
